description:
The exploration's first and possibly only step. With today's kernels, measure the cost of "state travels as binaries" against the kernel's own work:
- HLL-style: 16 KiB of registers in, 16 KiB out, per batch of 100 / 1k / 10k items (the ADR-0001 case; the HLL target workload defk-9p6.15 will reuse this).
- Bloom filter: 1 MiB and 16 MiB bit arrays, per batch of 1 / 100 / 10k inserts (needs defk-w38 for bit ops; until then simulate with byte-granular writes, which is a fair proxy for the copy cost).
- Streaming window: a 128 MB [u8] passed in and returned with one byte touched (the zstd/xxh3 streaming shape).

For each: time the kernel call end to end, and separately the memcpy-equivalent (alloc + copy + return of the same size, e.g. the `scale` kernel with k = 1.0), so the copy share is explicit. Note: an input binary is zero-copy in; the copy is the output allocation plus the copy of untouched bytes, so the share is (output copy) / (call time). Also record how the BEAM's own binary GC behaves with 16 MiB outputs at 10k calls/s (refc binary churn, :erlang.memory(:binary)).

Write the numbers into docs/research/state-copy-cost.md (branch research/state-copy-cost) with the per-size verdict: "value semantics is enough" where the share is under ~10%, and the sizes where it is not.

Done when: the document exists with measurements at the sizes above and a one-paragraph recommendation for the design review.

comments.text: Measured (bench/state_copy_cost.exs, docs/research/state-copy-cost.md; best of 7 interleaved, two runs, load 28-37, provisional; shares are back-to-back ratios). Copy = enif_alloc_binary + memcpy, same cost as :binary.copy (+~0.1 us): 0.35-0.39 us at 16 KiB, 14-15 us at 1 MiB, 260-300 us at 16 MiB, 2.2-2.5 ms at 128 MiB (55-75 GB/s). Share of call: HLL 16 KiB 75-83% / 30-33% / 4-5% at 100/1k/10k hashes (value semantics enough at 10k; in practice everywhere, 0.47 us vs Elixir 19 us at 100). Bloom 1 MiB ~100% / 95-100% / 20-25% at 1/100/10k inserts; 16 MiB ~100% / 94-100% / 87-89% (copy evicts the state: writes after it 4x slower than a warm no-copy twin). Window 128 MiB 100%, holds the scheduler 2.2-2.5 ms (no safepoint, defk-oed). Elixir :atomics Bloom beats today's kernel 170x (1 MiB) / 2700x (16 MiB) at 1 insert, 1.8x / 25x at 100; an in-place kernel would be 13-20x faster than :atomics from 100 inserts. GC: one GC per call, binary memory 1-2 states per process, nothing left after exit; 10k calls/s of 16 MiB unreachable (one process 3.7-3.8k/s, 12 procs 5-6.4k/s at 85-107 GB/s, 128-320 MiB live); a process holding 256 MiB of other binaries GCs every 4-5 calls and copies 1.6-2.2x slower. Recommendation: keep ADR-0001 for HLL-sized state; proceed to defk-sve.2 scoped to fixed-size single-owner buffers of ~1 MiB+ updated in small batches; weigh batching / block-split filters, and :atomics as a candidate Elixir meaning. Commit bf500ef on defk-sve.1/work.

title: Measure the per-call state copy cost at catalog sizes (value semantics vs in-place)
